$comment: Machine-readable claim ledger. A claim may only carry a proof level its evidence supports. LIVE_TESTNET requires a transaction hash a reader can check independently.

claims.claim: Usance core clearing contracts are deployed on X Layer testnet.
claims.detail: Ten contracts at commit 365eee5, first block 38596008. The verifier compares deployed runtime bytecode against what this checkout builds, so a manifest pointing at a superseded deployment fails instead of passing.

claims.claim: A Passport derived from a real issuer filing is committed onchain.
claims.detail: Franklin Templeton SEC Form 497K, CIK 1786958.

claims.claim: The committed Passport was verified by reading it back from the registry.
claims.detail: Version, assetId, evidenceRoot, claimsRoot, ACTIVE status and singleSource all compared against the candidate before any proof record was written.

claims.claim: ERC-8021 builder attribution is present on Usance X Layer writes.
claims.detail: Decoded back out of each submitted transaction's calldata, not assumed from the helper.

claims.claim: A risk epoch transition occurred onchain.
claims.detail: RiskEpoch is 5 on the current deployment, advanced by the committed Passport.

claims.claim: Collateral deposited onchain is recognised at a conservative value the protocol derives, not at market value.
claims.detail: 1000 tUSTB at $1 recognised as $980.13 — fixture S02, reproduced by a fourth independent deployment.

claims.claim: A borrow within the limit succeeds onchain.
claims.detail: $416.56 against $833.11 of capacity.

claims.claim: After a material risk deterioration, new borrowing is rejected by the contract.
claims.detail: Recognised value fell $980.13 to $490.07 and the account entered NO_NEW_RISK. A $10 borrow submitted with an explicit gas limit mined at block 38596307, burned 243878 gas, emitted no logs and reverted with AccountNotHealthy(1) — status 1 is NO_NEW_RISK.

claims.claim: Risk-reducing actions remain available while new risk is blocked.
claims.detail: Repay-all succeeded under NO_NEW_RISK, clearing debt to zero and returning the account to NORMAL.

claims.claim: A Passport cannot be committed onchain citing evidence that was never filed.
claims.detail: The deployed PassportRegistry checks every cited evidence id and recomputes the Merkle root. Evidence landed in block 38597280, the Passport in 38597284; reversing that order is a revert, not a convention.

claims.claim: Four independent implementations of the risk pipeline agree to the wei.
claims.detail: Solidity, Rust, TypeScript and a Python spec transcription over 28 scenarios spanning 6, 8 and 18 decimals. Mutation-verified.

claims.claim: A Passport built from one extraction path is capped and cannot claim corroboration.
claims.detail: singleSource because ChainGPT could not complete the extraction over a dense filing. The corroborator counts paths that produced a reading, not paths attempted.

claims.claim: A claim conflict cannot commit a Passport.
claims.detail: CLAIM_CONFLICT is a union variant with no candidate key, so committing one is a type error. Mutation-verified.

claims.claim: Real issuer documents are content-hashed and every digest recomputes from the stored bytes.
claims.detail: Franklin 2024/2025/2026, Arca, Ondo. rawDigest, contentHash, issuerId, sourceHash and evidenceId all recomputed.

claims.claim: An embedded prompt injection cannot reach a risk parameter.
claims.detail: Tested against the live model, which ignored the injection. The structural boundary holds regardless: no function reachable from an extractor sets a risk parameter.

claims.claim: Usance uses Chainlink Data Feeds on X Layer. Data Streams is not available there.
claims.detail: Corrects the planning material. Chainlink's registry lists X Layer with supportedFeatures feeds only.

claims.claim: Settlement-price freshness is explicitly configured and enforced for new risk.
claims.detail: ClearingHouse.settlementFreshness is {configured, maxAgeSeconds}. The deployed testnet value is 172,800s, two Chainlink heartbeats. Measured on X Layer mainnet: documented heartbeat 86,400s, worst observed gap 86,479s across 23 rounds of seven feeds, so a bound set at the heartbeat would reject honest feeds.

claims.claim: An unconfigured freshness policy cannot silently allow borrowing.
claims.detail: maxAge == 0 used to mean 'no bound', making never-configured and deliberately-unbounded the same state with the permissive reading shared between them. 14 tests; 6 mutations verified.

claims.claim: The evidence-to-Passport workflow survives restart and retry without double-committing.
claims.detail: Identity is derived from inputs, state is persisted atomically per workflow, and an unknown submission is resolved by reading the registry rather than resending. 32 tests; 8 mutations verified, including partial evidence confirmation counting as confirmed.

claims.claim: Three years of Franklin filings have a deterministic semantic-diff result.
claims.detail: 2024 to 2025 and 2025 to 2026 both classify NO_MATERIAL_CHANGE over 5 comparable fields, with the documents differing byte-for-byte. No deterioration was manufactured. The coverage denominator is reported because 5 of 17 is a weaker claim than 17 of 17.

claims.claim: Liquidation is progressive and routed on expected recovery.
claims.detail: Mined on X Layer testnet. An account walked NORMAL to NO_NEW_RISK to MARGIN_CALL as the collateral price fell, then 521.869 of 1000 tUSTB was seized — bounded by the close factor — retiring $390.59 of $791.46 debt and shrinking the breach from $85.77 to $63.46. The position was not closed and the account correctly remained MARGIN_CALL, because seizing collateral removes borrowing capacity as well as debt. Account state was never set directly.

claims.claim: Generated verification artifacts prove they describe the current world.
claims.detail: Every generated artifact carries provenance and consumers check it. A missing artifact is a failed run. Writes are atomic. 8 tests.

claims.claim: A single liquidation does not always cure a breach, and the protocol says so before acting.
claims.detail: Mined on X Layer testnet. The planner reported curesTheBreach=false and a $1,977.80 debt-to-cure against $791.46 of actual debt before acting, then the liquidation seized 521.869 tUSTB, retired $390.59, shrank the breach from $85.77 to $63.46, and correctly left the account MARGIN_CALL. Seizing collateral removes borrowing capacity as well as debt, so repair per dollar is 1-(1+t)m — about 0.05 at these parameters.

claims.claim: A cured account cannot be liquidated.
claims.detail: After repaying to NORMAL, a liquidation with identical arguments to the one that had just succeeded was refused. Eligibility is recomputed from live inputs on every call, so the same code path that authorised the first refuses the replay.

claims.claim: A liquidation route refuses to price a seizure off a stale oracle.
claims.detail: Elsewhere a stale price blocks a transaction; in a route it decides how much collateral leaves an account. isAvailable returns false rather than reverting, so one unusable route does not take the others down with it.

claims.claim: Real issuer tokens (FOBXX, OUSG, ARCOIN, xStocks) are usable as collateral.
claims.detail: tUSTB and tUSD are labelled testnet stand-ins with no relationship to any issuer.

claims.claim: Exchange OS / TradeZone execution.
claims.detail: No builder access.

claims.claim: LayerZero remote collateral.
claims.detail: Endpoint ids verified; contracts not built.

claims.claim: OKX DEX routing or qualifying interface volume.
claims.detail: No credentials, and attribution unconfirmed with the organiser.

claims.claim: Mainnet deployment.
Explorer-verified contract source.
claims.detail: Bytecode is live; source verification not yet attempted.

claims.claim: A corroborated (two-path) Franklin Passport.
claims.detail: Blocked by the ChainGPT gateway limit on dense filings.

claims.claim: Third-party liquidators are paid an explicit incentive out of liquidation proceeds.
claims.detail: Mined on X Layer testnet by keeper 0xac575403, an address distinct from the borrower and holding only the LIQUIDATOR role. Of 413.320249 tUSD of route proceeds, the keeper received 20.666012 (5.000%), the treasury 0xDd280E77 received 2.066601 (0.500%), and 390.587636 (94.500%) retired debt. The three destinations account for every unit, measured by onchain balance delta. Before this the whole amount retired the borrower's own debt, so no third party had any reason to liquidate anything.

claims.claim: Protocol fees are bounded by constants that governance cannot raise.
claims.detail: Every ceiling is a Solidity constant, not a settable parameter: governance that can raise its own limit has no limit. The liquidator incentive and the protocol liquidation fee are also bounded jointly, because two individually-safe parameters can be ruinous together. Not yet exercised against a governance attack on a live deployment, so this is UNIT_TESTED.

claims.claim: A vault whose capital is lent out queues redemptions rather than promising instant liquidity.
claims.detail: withdraw() pays only what is genuinely free; anything else joins a FIFO queue that is senior to new lending. Shares burn when the request is made, so a later default cannot shrink a claim that already exited, and cancelling reissues at today's price rather than the price when queued. Queued cash is excluded from availableCash and queued liabilities from NAV, so the same money is never offered to two parties. Not yet exercised on a live deployment.

claims.claim: Protocol reserves absorb the first loss before lenders do.
claims.detail: recordBadDebt spends the reserve before writing anything down against lender NAV. A protocol that accumulates a reserve out of borrower interest and then socialises the first loss anyway has charged a fee for insurance it did not provide. Losses beyond the reserve are borne by lenders in that vault only — there is no cross-vault socialisation, because a lender who chose one asset's risk did not choose another's.

claims.claim: Delegated authority is the intersection of protocol policy and a user-signed mandate.
claims.detail: Mined on X Layer testnet. Owner 0xBA813263 signed a mandate granting REPAY only to agent 0xCe805513, a distinct address. The agent repaid $50 from its own balance through DelegationGateway and the owner's debt fell from $150 to $100.01. Both the mandate check and the protocol path had to pass; neither can satisfy the call alone.

claims.claim: An agent cannot withdraw user collateral.
claims.detail: Refused onchain at block 38638066. The same agent that had just performed a permitted repayment attempted a collateral outflow under the same mandate; the transaction was submitted with an explicit gas limit so the refusal was mined rather than caught at estimation, and it reverted in a block anybody can look up. Enforced twice: the mandate vocabulary has no outflow verb, and DelegationGateway reverts on every action it does not name.

claims.claim: Autonomous borrowing is refused rather than shipped half-wired.
claims.detail: BORROW is in the mandate vocabulary and the registry checks its debt ceiling correctly, but ClearingHouse refuses to delegate it with ActionNotDelegable. Enabling it requires every bound wired end to end; shipping it half-checked to look complete is the failure this layer exists to prevent.

claims.claim: Revocation ends a delegated agent's authority, and the refusal is mined onchain.
claims.detail: Mined on X Layer testnet. Owner 0xBA813263 signed a REPAY-only mandate to agent 0xCe805513, a distinct address; the agent repaid, the owner revoked, and the same agent's identical next attempt reverted in a block. isLive read true before the revocation and false after. The retry was submitted with an explicit gas limit so the refusal was mined rather than caught at estimation — a revert nobody can look up is not proof the protocol refused anything. The refused attempt did not reduce the debt; the only movement between the two blocks was accrued interest.

claims.claim: The Usance Sentinel registries are deployed on X Layer testnet, additively beside the core.
claims.detail: SentinelTemplateRegistry at 0xd8e1c67c and SentinelInstanceRegistry at 0x882c941a, deployed against the existing Authority. No core contract was redeployed; the registries hold no role over any money contract.

claims.claim: A Sentinel template is committed with immutable versioning and an instance pins it, onchain.
claims.detail: T1 Safety Buffer committed as templateId 0x0dbe0105 v1 (RISK_REDUCING_ONLY). An instance registered as 0xb7124e96, pinning templateId, version and manifest hash. The InstanceRegistered event carries the pin.

claims.claim: A Sentinel instance cannot bind a template whose committed manifest it does not match — the refusal is mined onchain.
claims.detail: A registerInstance carrying a mismatched manifest hash was submitted with an explicit gas limit and reverted in a block with ManifestMismatch (selector 0xe07a5886), status 0. This is the onchain half of I-62: an instance's pin is verified, not assumed.

claims.claim: Every Sentinel financial action requires both protocol and mandate authorization, and the autonomy plane cannot widen its own bounds.
claims.detail: Invariants I-60..I-74. The engine end-to-end proves duplicate triggers produce one effect (I-63), execution-unknown releases nothing (I-64), a moved epoch blocks (I-65), a weak/AI trigger cannot increase risk (I-66), and a revoked mandate blocks (I-73); the contract tests prove immutable versions, pin integrity (I-62) and no money role (I-61). Mutation guards recorded in docs/SENTINELS_SECURITY.md §4.

claims.claim: A Sentinel autonomously repaid debt on X Layer without a user initiating the transaction.
claims.detail: Mined on X Layer testnet at block 38767411. The Sentinel engine observed the account through live viem adapters, compiled a risk-reducing REPAY, checked ProtocolAllows ∧ MandateAllows against the live epoch and mandate state, and the bounded agent executor 0xCe805513 — distinct from the owner 0xBA813263 — submitted the repayment through DelegationGateway. The owner's debt fell 0.02913 -> 0.01913 tUSD and no human sent the transaction (run 0xc29b11e6, instance 0xb7124e96). New borrowing was separately refused with AccountNotHealthy because the testnet mock feeds are stale, which is why a standing debt was reduced rather than freshly created: REPAY is risk-reducing and remains available while new risk is gated. The loop is also proven offline in engine.test.ts.
